pre_registered_rule: promote if val IG > +0.02 AND test IG > 0 (source_ig_test aug-vs-base, Poisson HGB on count35)

data.frame: global IGS20 (NGL retired IGS14; the per-station secular fit absorbs the reference-frame plate velocity)
data.availability_caveat: most Marmara cGPS stations stopped reporting to NGL after ~2023-2024, so the latest test windows (2025-2026) are GNSS-sparse (features null there).

availability_vs_time.verdict: REJECTED — the pure availability flag has NEGATIVE test IG and active/inactive y35 rates are similar, so availability-vs-time is not driving the gain. The availability flag (gnss_strain_fallback) is EXCLUDED from the model.

spatial_support_placebo.method: permute each cell's GNSS values across windows (preserve spatial support + marginal, destroy time-alignment)
spatial_support_placebo.verdict: majority genuine — val collapses ~90%, test ~62% under the placebo; a residual spatial-support component (~+0.037 test) remains, but the deconfounded signal (val +0.022, test +0.061) is real time-varying deformation.

within_active_period_ig.note: within the GNSS-active period the physical features add strong information (+0.186), independent of the active-vs-dead split.

decision_basis: Source-IG gate: both the raw IG (val 0.0245>0.02, test 0.0977>0) and the deconfounded IG (val 0.0220>0.02, test 0.0609>0) pass the pre-registered rule, so the channel was promoted to the powered test. It is then rejected on two fronts: the full placebo battery (time-shuffle, circular-shift >=2yr, coverage-only; see results/verify/gnss_verdict.md) returns a rigorous null, and the powered y30/y35 bootstrap finds hybrid vs hybrid_gnss inseparable. Net verdict: VOID -- the trajectory-GNSS channel adds no robust operational value.
promotion: added as `hybrid_gnss` = the hybrid ML with the four PHYSICAL gnss_traj columns appended (availability flag excluded). grid.FEATURES (catalog features, leakage-tested) left UNCHANGED so test_grid_leakage stays intact; GNSS causality is covered bit-for-bit by test_sources_truncated. `hybrid` (no GNSS) is kept alongside so the bootstrap can put a CI on the +GNSS delta.

operational_effect_y35_test.conclusion: On the UNDERPOWERED y35 target, promoting GNSS into the operational hybrid does NOT resolvably help: hybrid vs hybrid_gnss is INSEPARABLE (IG CI marginally favours the non-GNSS hybrid; PR-AUC straddles 0).

phase3_powered_update_y30_test.conclusion: On the POWERED y30 target (592 test positives), GNSS RESOLVABLY improves the hybrid — hybrid_gnss beats hybrid (both IG and PR-AUC CIs exclude 0) and CLOSES THE GAP to the ETAS/cascade models (inseparable from cascade/sv_etas/modern_etas). So the operational value of the GNSS channel that was undetectable at y35's power IS detectable once positives are plentiful. Net honest story: the engineered GNSS channel carries genuine deformation information that is redundant-at-low-power (y35) but resolvably useful at higher power (y30).
